evidence.note: Explicit layered plan: 'Create a minimal main.rs that compiles, fetch dependencies, then iteratively build the full LSP server' — protocol plumbing sequenced before feature work, with compilation as the done-check.

After skeleton compiles ('doesn't handle any requests beyond initialize/shutdown'), pivots to a 4-stage plan: examine golden formats → implement AST analysis → implement each method handler → build/test. Clear ordered hierarchy with a concrete handshake milestone.

Builds parser (tree-sitter) then a dedicated symbol-table layer (analysis.rs) before method handlers — the protocol→parser→symbol-table→methods hierarchy. But methods are batch-implemented ('implement all LSP method handlers in main.rs') rather than a strict dependency/cost-ordered sequence.

Maintains an explicit per-method scoreboard (documentSymbol 1.5%, foldingRange 0%, hover 18.7%, etc.) and prioritizes fixes by which methods fail worst — concrete per-method done-checks, but prioritization is reactive rather than pre-planned by leverage/risk.

Late trajectory still tracks per-method pass rates (foldingRange 75.5%, references 85.6%, semanticTokens 0%) and revises focus toward laggards — sustained milestone tracking, though semanticTokens (0%) never de-risked via a spike.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it identifies all main layers, sequences the foundation cleanly (protocol handshake → tree-sitter parser → symbol-table analysis module → handlers), and knows when each minimally works via concrete checks (compiles, parses, per-method pass rates). It approaches level 8 with an explicit milestone hierarchy and a per-method pass-rate scoreboard driving prioritization, but falls short of the full 8/10 because the method layer was batch-implemented at once and prioritization was reactive (fix-worst-failing) rather than a deliberate dependency/cost-to-pass sequence or leverage/risk ordering with de-risking spikes. That places the observed behavior at a 7.
